query: How can we design MIS architecture and data governance (access controls, privacy, retention, interoperability with cadastral systems) while planning for limited cadastral access?

response.query: How can we design MIS architecture and data governance (access controls, privacy, retention, interoperability with cadastral systems) while planning for limited cadastral access?
response.answer: Design MIS architecture with strict access controls, privacy measures, and data retention policies. Use spatial data trusts for interoperability, even with limited cadastral access. Ensure compliance with security and privacy regulations.

results.title: Spatial data trusts: an emerging governance framework for ...
results.content: However, the data Trust governance approach is still relatively unexplored for managing, protecting, and sharing spatial data. (Citation2020) identified five main requirements for establishing a successful data Trust: (i) to satisfy a legal framework for facilitating, protecting, and sharing data; (ii) to be an accountable and transparent data governing body; (iii) to provide well defined and organized guidelines and policies for data management; (iv) to enforce data beneficiaries to comply with data Trust agreements and policies; and (v) to enable an early, effective, and direct relationship with public and relevant stakeholders. illustrates an example of proposed spatial data Trust and its effective role in managing, protecting, and sharing personal location data. While a relatively new data governance model today, we anticipate that spatial data Trusts will play a central role in protecting, mediating, and enabling spatial data sharing between a range of key stakeholders in the future.
